entries.jsdocSummary: Advisory locks inside a transaction you already have. The lock lives until that transaction ends; `release` only forgets the grant. Given a savepoint handle (a nested `tx.transaction`), a ROLLBACK of that savepoint frees the lock at once, while the outer transaction goes on. Postgres advisory locks are re-entrant within one session, so a second acquire of the same key on the same transaction succeeds: exclusion is between transactions. That holds for read/write too: a read followed by a write of the same key in ONE transaction is granted (Postgres lets one session take both), so there is no upgrade check here.

The target is fixed when you call it. * Do not await it when a callback hangs on purpose. */ advance(duration: Duration): Promise<void>; /** How many timers are waiting to fire. */ readonly pendingTimers: number; };
